label: prop:descent-eigenspaces
title: Eigenspaces of the descent involution
html:
Proposition. Eigenspaces of the descent involution

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes the level-(n{+}1) endomorphism algebra into a direct sum:

  \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1})
  = 
  \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}}  \oplus  \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}},

where \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n is the descended subalgebra (endomorphisms that factor through level n) and \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n is the transient complement (genuinely new endomorphisms at level n{+}1). The algebraic filter (algebraic filter) refines this decomposition:

  1. Bosonic modes. Longitudinal modes lifted from level n lie entirely in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}}. They commute with the curvature and survive every round-trip through the tower.
  2. Fermionic modes. Ladder modes at level n{+}1 split between the two summands. Those in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} are the modes created by the jet prolongation that lack a pre-image at level n.
